text:
elaine (CEO): Quick weekly snapshot from me — a few high-priority asks and a short readout. TL;DR: EU Dedicated beta next Wed, cost push on hosted, and a small incident postmortem. Full notes: https://redwood-internal.link/weekly-snapshot-2187 :spiral_calendar:

samir (VP Product): noted. Can we confirm the EU beta feature list? We have to lock the telemetry and rollout toggles by EOD Tuesday. I'll post the final checklist in the doc.

elaine (CEO): yes — samir please own rollout toggles + canary config. Jess, marco — eng owners for SLA targets and fallback policy?

jess (Head of Eng): taking SLA ownership. I'll coordinate canary windows with infra. Initial target: 99.9% availability for API surface, p99 generation latency <= 120ms for standard text-gen (non-stream). Will validate against replay tests tomorrow morning.

marco (CTO): I'll handle fallback policy and model-variant routing for capacity pressure. Plan: primary model -> quantized fallback -> smaller-flavor fallback. Also we should enable automatic region failover in the blueprint for EU dedicated.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: rollout-dedicated-eu v1 -> canary @ 2026-03-25T08:00Z. Canary window: 2h. Auto-rollback threshold: 3% error spike or >150ms p95 latency.

elaine (CEO): On cost — Optimize team proposed config changes that should net ~12% per-token savings on hosted by applying mixed quant profiles + smarter batching heuristics. Samir, please prioritize the A/B on high-volume routes.

samir (VP Product): On it. We'll pick two high-volume routes (chat-stream and single-shot-longprompt) and run a 48h A/B. If quality regression <= 0.5% we switch.

alex (Sales): Heads-up: we told two pilot customers in EU they'd get dedicated access next week. Sales needs final confirmation of traffic limits and SLA wording for the contracts. Samir + Jess — can you DM details after this thread?

anya (People Ops): Small operational note: we're pausing all non-critical offsites for the next two weeks to keep engineers available for launch and support. If a team has a critical + approved reason, ping me.

elaine (CEO): Incident summary (brief): Friday 17:22 UTC we had degraded KV-cache hits affecting tail latency; root cause: autoscaler race when a rolling upgrade triggered kernel-level page reclaim leading to cache eviction. Impact window ~18m, ~0.6% of requests experienced >500ms token latency. No customer data exposure.

jess (Head of Eng): Postmortem draft: https://redwood-internal.link/pm-kv-cache-2026-03-20 — primary fixes: sequence-lock on rolling upgrades, tighter memory headroom defaults, and an emergency fallback that disables KV-prefetch if page reclaim detected. Action owners in the doc.

marco (CTO): Also adding a lightweight probe in the scheduler to detect reclaim pressure and delay low-priority batch spawns. Will PR today.

elaine (CEO): Requests from me:
- samir: finalize A/B routes + contract wording with Alex
- jess: confirm replay pass and canary dashboard by 06:00 UTC Wed
- marco: PR for scheduler probe + doc the fallback plan
- anya: communicate resourcing pause and escalation path to teams

samir (VP Product): Affirmative. I'll update the doc and ping Alex.

jess (Head of Eng): Replay scheduled, will post link to canary dashboard once ready.

marco (CTO): PR created: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5421 — tagged for review.

alex (Sales): Thanks — I'll hold customers to soft confirmation until you DM me.

elaine (CEO): Final note: big thanks to the infra and runtime teams for the rapid triage on Friday. We'll keep the cadence of these weekly flash notes; next one will include a short cost dashboard snapshot. :heart: 

samir (VP Product): Appreciated. Short ask — anyone seeing blockers with EU compliance checklist, DM me.

deploy-bot: Canary completed: no rollback triggered. Metrics: error spike 0.7% at 08:12Z (below threshold), p95 118ms.

jess (Head of Eng): Closing loop — will run a quick post-canary incident review tomorrow.

elaine (CEO): Great work. If no other flags, I'm closing this thread. Ping me for any escalation. :rocket:
